title: Adaptive token-bubble simulator and phase-aligned aggregator
author: Anya Patel
commits: init: add token-bubble simulator core loop and config plumbing
feat: implement phase-aligned trace aggregator and export CSV/HTML

description: Context: We observed intermittent microbursts in mixed-sequence workloads where short 'token bubbles' produce misleading aggregated p95/p99 numbers when aligned naively across sessions. Motivation: Provide a lightweight simulator to synthesize token-bubble patterns and a phase-aligned aggregator to produce stable per-kernel latency baselines that account for intra-sequence token alignment. Goals: 1) enable reproducible synthetic bursts that mirror frontend priming patterns; 2) compute phase-aligned aggregation so latency summaries do not conflate alignment artifacts; 3) produce easy-to-consume HTML and CSV reports for the benchmark lab dashboard. Summary of changes: Adds a Python-based simulator that supports programmable session templates, sequence mixes, and configurable bubble amplitude/duration; adds a Go aggregator that ingests per-token traces and aligns events by sequence phase before computing pXX/tail metrics; adds an integration test harness and CI pipeline stage to run the simulation+aggregation end-to-end; includes documentation and a short runbook for interpreting results. How to run: see bench/reports/README at root for quickstart; curl-based example included that runs the simulator with 1000 sessions and produces token_bubble_report.html. Checklist: [x] simulator core implemented [x] aggregator implemented [x] integration test added [x] CI stage wired [x] docs and runbook added. Impact: This PR improves fidelity of baseline measurements for workloads with interleaved short and long sequences and will be used as part of the nightly baseline suite and by performance investigations. Related work: references ENG-1267 for regression triage and ENG-1302 for dashboard integration. Notes: no production-facing API changes, strictly bench tooling.
